root_cause.text: Insufficient validation of the `ErrorDataLength` field in SMB2 error responses allows a crafted large value to cause pointer arithmetic wrap-around on 32-bit architectures, leading to an infinite loop or out-of-bounds read in the `symlink_data()` function.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (len > end - ((u8 *)p + sizeof(*p)))` to prevent using a length that would exceed the available buffer. The CVE description explicitly shows that values like `0xfffffff8` and `0xfffffff0` cause the pointer `next` to wrap back to `p` or before `p` on 32-bit systems, resulting in an infinite loop or out-of-bounds read.
